policy: Conjunctive clearance: (1) released before 1931 — US public domain by age; (2) item date corroborates the release year; (3) no youtube rips or banned collections; (4) a playable h.264 file. License tags are supporting evidence only.

clips.title: A Railway Collision
clips.blurb: Walter R. Booth wrecks two model trains on a mountain ledge — the oldest staged catastrophe in the dataset, forty-eight seconds of engineered calamity.
clips.what: Model trains meet head-on beside a tunnel mouth; carriages tumble down the slope.

source.file: A Railway Collision 1900 Directed by Walter R. Booth .mp4

source.note: Duplicate upload "silent-a-railway-collision" (curated silent_films collection, same 1900 date) corroborates identity.

clips.title: Searching Ruins on Broadway, Galveston, for Dead Bodies
clips.blurb: Eight days after the deadliest hurricane in American history, an Edison crew set a tripod among the debris of Broadway. Disaster cinema before anyone thought to invent it: the camera simply arrived.
clips.what: Work crews pick through the wreckage of the Galveston hurricane, September 1900.

source.file: Searching Ruins on Broadway, Galveston, for Dead Bodies.mp4
source.pdBasis: Released 1900; US public domain — published before 1931.

clips.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 1
clips.blurb: Not on the film list — raw reels from the Prelinger Archives. Refugees, tent kitchens and freestanding chimneys: the same catastrophe at street level, unedited.
clips.what: Displaced residents and ruined buildings; the original print jumps and rolls.

source.pdBasis: Released 1906; US public domain — published before 1931.

clips.title: San Francisco: Aftermath of Earthquake
clips.blurb: The dataset’s first earthquake: actuality reels shot in the smouldering weeks after 18 April 1906, cut together from the footage that survived.
clips.what: Pans across ruined San Francisco streets, toppled facades and burned-out blocks.
clips.audioNote: Silent footage — the score on this transfer was added by the compiler.

source.pdBasis: Released 1906; US public domain — published before 1931.
source.note: Item carries no date field. Identity rests on content: every foot of it is 1906 San Francisco aftermath actuality, matching the dataset film. The uploader states it is a compilation of those reels with a music track added, and licenses that edit CC BY 3.0.

clips.title: The Sinking of the Lusitania
clips.blurb: Winsor McCay spent nearly two years drawing the torpedoing of the Lusitania — some 25,000 drawings. The first animated documentary, and still furious.
clips.what: Animated re-enactment: the liner steams into frame, the torpedo strikes, the ship goes down by the bow.
clips.audioNote: Silent picture — any sound on this transfer is an added score.

source.pdBasis: Released 1918; US public domain — published before 1931.
source.note: A second upload ("Sinking_of_the_Lusitania", also dated 1918) corroborates identity; it was rejected for carrying a spurious NC-ND tag.

clips.title: Sodom and Gomorrah
clips.blurb: Michael Curtiz, two decades before Casablanca, burns a biblical city with thousands of Viennese extras. The oldest divine judgment on the books.
clips.what: Fire rains on the city; crowds flee through collapsing colonnades; the ruins smoke.
clips.audioNote: Silent picture — any sound on this transfer is an added score.

source.pdBasis: Released 1922; US public domain — published before 1931.
source.note: Item date 1923-03-26 is the general release; the premiere was October 1922 (dataset year). Duplicate upload "sodom-und-gomorrha-lucy-doraine" (dated 1922, named for its star) corroborates identity.

clips.title: The White Sister
clips.blurb: Lillian Gish takes the veil; Vesuvius objects. A romantic melodrama that settles its third act with an eruption and a burst dam.
clips.what: The climax: the volcano erupts, the dam gives way, and tinted crowds evacuate into the smoke.
clips.audioNote: Silent picture — any sound on this transfer is an added score.

source.pdBasis: Released 1923; US public domain — published before 1931.

clips.title: The Johnstown Flood
clips.blurb: Fox’s dramatisation of the 1889 dam failure that killed 2,209 people. The dataset files it under Floods; Pennsylvania filed it under memory.
clips.what: The South Fork dam gives way and the flood takes the valley below.
clips.audioNote: Silent picture — any sound on this transfer is an added score.

source.pdBasis: Released 1926; US public domain — published before 1931.
source.note: A second 1926-dated transfer ("the-johnstown-flood", 66 min vs 68 min here) corroborates identity; it was passed over for a TCM broadcast bug burned into the frame.

clips.title: Noah's Ark
clips.blurb: Warner Bros. answers the Great War with the Great Flood. The deluge was real enough to injure stuntmen; sound was arriving, and so was the water.
clips.what: Lightning splits the rock; the storm builds toward the breaking of the flood.
clips.audioNote: Part-talkie — synchronised score with talking sequences.

source.pdBasis: Released 1928; US public domain — published before 1931.

clips.title: Madam Satan
clips.blurb: Cecil B. DeMille throws a masquerade aboard a zeppelin, then hits it with a storm. The last film here to enter the public domain — 1 January 2026.
clips.what: The costume ball in the dirigible; the storm; the guests take to parachutes.
clips.audioNote: Sound film — original recorded dialogue and score.
